text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: GPU pool 'west-eu-rt-1' effective capacity degraded by 48%. Autoscaler hit scale_limit and failing to recover. Symptoms: queue growth on /generate, increased 5xxs and timeouts. Paging SRE.

mike-oncall: On it. seeing queue backlog ~12k requests, 95th latency spiking to 6.2s. Any node flaps or driver errors in logs?

ana-sre: Driver logs show repeated CUDA/Xid 31 and Xid 79 across multiple nodes, followed by GPU process OOMs. Node metrics show GPUs going into 'unavailable' state then flapping back. Autoscaler refused new instances due to policy scale_limit=20 (we're at 20).

sara-eng: Is this originating from a new model? Recent rollout?

joel-ops: No model rollout. We got an increase in small, high-concurrency traffic from a partner at 08:53 UTC that raised average batch depth. Likely exposing a driver memory fragmentation bug.

mike-oncall: Immediate actions: 1) throttle non-prod routes 2) evict low-priority jobs 3) fallback to smaller model variant 4) open customer impact thread. Who can take each?

courtney-cs: I'll start impact ping. Early signal: three customers reported timeouts in EU region, one reduction in SLA. I'll collect request ids.

ana-sre: Technical mitigation I can do now: cordon two most unstable nodes, restart nvidia-driver/daemonset on them, and force kube-scheduler to reschedule pods off flaky GPUs. Commands I'll run:
```bash
kubectl cordon gpu-node-12
kubectl drain gpu-node-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data -n inference
kubectl rollout restart daemonset/nvidia-driver -n kube-system
```
I'll also set autoscaler max to +5 temporarily to allow headroom, but need approval.

joel-ops: Approve bump to max=25 for 30m as emergency. Make sure we have capacity in billing pool. If that doesn't help, we'll fallback to warm standby region (west-us).

mike-oncall: Approved. ana, apply change and monitor queue depth. Also enable autoscaler fallback policy to allow launching CPU-based fallback instances for short requests.

ana-sre: Done: increased max to 25, enabled fallback to cpu-fallback class. Watching scale events. Also pushed a temporary autoscaler rule to favor new nodes with driver kernel parameter 'no_cc_major' disabled (avoid a known kernel/driver race).

sara-eng: On the app side I'm enabling prefix-KV cache for common prompts and forcing 1.5s client-side timeout to cut retry storms. Pushing patch to route config now.

courtney-cs: Customer update: EU payments partner saw 30% failed requests between 08:55-09:05 UTC. We're contacting their engineering lead and offering mitigation steps.

mike-oncall: Quick health checks: 1) Are there any nodes reporting GPU memory errors (OOM) without Xid recovery? 2) any long-running traces stuck on KV cache miss?

ana-sre: Yes, gpu-node-09 logged repeated "GPU OOM during kernel execution" and then Xid 79. I restarted the node and it rejoined healthy. Node-12 and Node-15 are still flapping.

joel-ops: Evicted non-critical batch jobs from pool and moved queued requests to cpu-fallback where possible. That shaved ~3k from the GPU queue.

mike-oncall: Good. Next: perform rolling restart of driver daemonset on remaining suspect nodes during low-traffic windows. Coordinate with infra to avoid simultaneous restarts. Also open a ticket to vendor with driver traces.

ana-sre: Creating vendor ticket with attached /var/log/nvidia* and dmesg dumps. Example snippet:
```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (79): GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 1234.568901] kernel: nvidia 0000:65:00.0: GPU is lost
```

mike-oncall: Customer comms: courtney, please send interim note: we've mitigated most of the queue, escalated vendor, and expect further stabilization in 30-45 minutes. Offer rate-limiting tips for clients.

courtney-cs: Sent. They acknowledged and asked for ETA on full recovery.

sara-eng: I'm preparing a lightweight model fallback plan for the SDK to automatically switch to a 6B quantized variant for latency-sensitive calls. Will push opt-in flag to SDK in 20m.

ana-sre: Autoscaler has launched 3 new nodes (max 25), but two immediately reported driver init failures and were evicted by node-problem-detector. We need to avoid churn. I'll set the autoscaler cooldown to 4m and disable concurrent launches >1 for now.

mike-oncall: Do that. Also capture core dumps from GPU processes for postmortem. Use this helper:
```bash
kubectl exec -n inference -it $(kubectl get po -l app=inference -o name | head -n1) -- bash -c 'gcore -o /tmp/core $(pidof model_server)'
```

joel-ops: Noted. I'll coordinate storage for core bundles and upload to S3: s3://redwood-debug/gpu-flare/4512349876/

courtney-cs: Customers updated: two on high-priority plans were routed to fallback region; they confirmed degraded but functional service. One said they saw resumed requests ~09:12 UTC.

mike-oncall: Status check @09:17 UTC: queue down to 2.1k, 95th latency 2.1s, error rate down to baseline. Still some GPU nodes showing Xid but fewer. Need to keep monitoring and begin post-incident actions: rollback any aggressive autoscaler changes, collect metrics for RCA, and prepare an incident postmortem.

ana-sre: Agree. I'll keep the emergency max=25 until we have vendor root cause. If stable for 1 hour, we'll revert. Collecting logs and traces now.

sara-eng: I'll tag the SDK fallback PR as "hotfix" so we can land quickly if vendor fix is delayed.

mike-oncall: Oncall handoff in 30m to ana-sre shift. I'm writing initial incident notes and timeline. Anyone else to add?

joel-ops: Added list of affected nodes and exact pod evictions to the thread artifacts in the incident tracker.

courtney-cs: I'll follow up with customers after vendor reply and keep CS updates in sync.

incident-bot: Incident recorded: #INC-2026-4512349876. Severity: P2 -> customer impact reported, partial mitigation in place. Channels: incidents, infra-alerts.

mike-oncall: Thanks everyone. If anything spikes again, ping @mike-oncall and @ana-sre. Closing live coordination; monitoring continues.
